messages:
Emma L: Heads-up — onboarding flow hit a gem conflict in the sampleapp when I tried to use ruby-sdk 2.4.0.rc1. Gemfile pins 2.3.x and bundler refuses to resolve. Anyone run into this?

Raj P: Can you paste the Gemfile snippet and the exact bundler error?

Emma L: Sure — here's the relevant part:
```
# Gemfile
gem "redwood-rb", "~> 2.3.0"
```
Error is basically: `Bundler could not find compatible versions for gem "redwood-rb": conflict between 2.3.x and 2.4.0.rc1` and an initializer trace pointing at `RetryPolicy.new(...)`.

Morgan S: Seeing the same on CI for the sampleapp-test job — 2.4.0.rc1 fails with a method arity/kwarg error in the retry ctor. Quick trace: `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 2, expected 1)` from lib/redwood/retry.rb

Jules: We did change the retry API in 2.4 (keyword args -> single options object) to make behavior explicit. That is a breaking change. Two paths: revert to a backward-compatible ctor or update the sampleapp to the new API. For onboarding we should keep sampleapp working.

Emma L: +1 to keeping onboarding friction low. If you can add a tiny compatibility shim in the SDK that maps the old signatures to the new one that'd be great. I can open the sampleapp PR if we decide to bump.

Jules: I'll prepare a small maintenance PR on the SDK side that provides `RetryPolicy.new(*args)` fallback which normalizes to the new interface and logs a deprecation. Will link it here.

devex-bot: CI: sampleapp-tests #342 failed — https://ci.redwood/342 

Raj P: Also add a note in the release/changelog that 2.4 changed retry API and onboarding sampleapp may need a bump. We should include a one-liner remediation in the upgrade notes.

Morgan S: For a short-term local workaround: `bundle update redwood-rb --conservative` or pin bundler to an older minor (if lockfile mismatch). But that's brittle; prefer the shim + changelog.

Emma L: Thanks all — I'll hold off on the sampleapp PR until Jules posts the SDK shim PR, then I'll test locally and push an updated sampleapp dependency bump. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
